subject: Operational simulations and fallback-binding agreement
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@evergreenbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@evergreenbank.com
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: operational simulations and binding fallback ask

Jordan,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. As part of our operational risk review we need two pieces of evidence from vendors: a) a summary of how you perform multi-region outage simulations (schedule, blackout scope, success criteria) and b) a fallback-binding clause that commits a vendor to an operational remediation / migration path if a regional outage impacts our production traffic.

Attached is our short questionnaire and an outline of the fallback clause language we typically ask for. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Participate in a 2-hour simulated regional failover with a pre-negotiated RPO/RTO test matrix within Q4;
- Provide a draft fallback-binding agreement (non-standard commercial ask for us) so our procurement team can review redlines;

We'd like a response by EOD 2026-10-08 so procurement can evaluate alongside the rest of the RFP.

Regards,
Carlos
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Evergreen Bank

Attachment: evergreen-rfp-operational-q.pdf (stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: operational simulations and binding fallback ask

Carlos,

Thanks — we can do this. High-level reply below; internal folks on this thread to provide technical/legal detail so we can deliver the draft by your deadline.

Summary:
- Simulation participation: yes. We run quarterly multi-region outage drills for hosted customers and can schedule a scoped 2-hour simulation in Q4.
- RTO/RPO: our standard supported SLAs are RTO <= 15 minutes for session continuity (with traffic routing) and RPO <= 0 seconds for KV/metadata with our async replication; for longer-running stateful workloads we provide documented recovery sequencing with target RPOs (see attached excerpt).
- Fallback-binding draft: we have an internal template for operational fallback commitments; it requires legal review for procurement-level binding language. We'll circulate a draft fallback-terms doc for your review by 2026-10-08.

Next steps (internal): Karthik — can you confirm the exact RTO/RPO language we should put in the draft and any caveats for customer-run simulations (data privacy, cross-region snapshot retention)? Laura — procurement and legal notes: what level of binding language have we accepted historically for similar requests?

Jordan
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: operational simulations and binding fallback ask

Jordan / Carlos — technical details below. I'll keep this targeted for procurement language, but happy to hop on a call if you want the architecture walk-through.

Simulation approach (what we run for customers):
- Scope: simulate region (us-west-2) complete outage for 2 hours; control-plane and data-plane traffic routed to secondary region (us-east-1).
- Pre-reqs: test keys, a short traffic steering window, and a no-production-change window agreed in advance.
- Success criteria (we measure): DNS failover time, p95 request latency post-failover, transactional tail-loss rate, consumer KV cache warm-up time.

RTO/RPO specifics for the draft:
- RTO: We target a measured customer-facing request continuity RTO of <= 30s for non-streaming stateless requests when automated routing is enabled; for stateful conversational sessions RTO is measured as the time to restore conversation continuity (KV warm-up + model cache) and is target <= 3 minutes in our standard production profile.
- RPO: For ephemeral session state we maintain an in-memory KV cache with asynchronous replication; we can commit to an operational RPO of <= 60 seconds for in-memory session reconstruction in the fallback-binding draft. For durable storage (user transcripts, embeddings persisted to customer storage) RPO depends on customer-side ingestion window — we'll call this out as a dependent factor.

Caveats to include in the fallback-binding draft:
- Cross-region data transfers during simulation may be subject to customer's data residency policies; we will not persist test data beyond the simulation without explicit permission.
- Third-party network failures and cloud provider region-level persistence guarantees are out-of-scope; our commitment will be operational (perform the migration steps and provide a runbook and assisted execution) rather than an absolute restoration SLA for provider-level catastrophic loss.

Attachments: operational-simulations.pdf (internal test checklist stub)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: operational simulations and binding fallback ask

Jordan / Karthik — legal/procurement notes for the draft fallback-binding doc:

Key points for Redwood's procurement team to expect:
- We can accept operational commitments (we will execute a defined failover playbook, provide runbook artifacts, and participate in scheduled simulations), but we require the language to be framed as "Operational Commitment" rather than an unconditional indemnity or monetary SLA tied to customer loss.
- Suggested wording: commit to perform defined migration/remediation actions within specified timeboxes and provide escalation/resolution support; allow a carve-out for cloud-provider catastrophic events and for customer configuration errors.
- We'll include a change-control clause: any binding commitment requires mutual sign-off on the simulation scope and success criteria prior to execution.

Procurement ask: Jordan, please prepare a draft "fallback-terms-draft.docx" with the operational commitment language and the scope/caveats above. Copy me when you send to the customer so we can track redlines.

Laura
VP, Legal Ops & Procurement
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: procurement@evergreenbank.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: fallback-binding terms and simulation plan (redwood)

Carlos — attached is our draft fallback-terms and an operational simulation checklist / proposed timeline for the 2-hour test. High-level callouts:

- We frame this as an "Operational Commitment" with explicit caveats for provider-level catastrophes and customer-configured persistence.
- RTO/RPO commitments included as operational targets: RTO <= 3 minutes for session continuity (measured), RPO <= 60 seconds for reconstructable ephemeral state.
- Pre-simulation signoff required: scope, test keys, data residency constraints, and a runbook acceptance sign-off at least 5 business days before the test.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-10-20: mutual sign-off on scope & success criteria; procurement sends any initial redlines
- 2026-11-03: dry run with staging traffic only (internal observers)
- 2026-11-10: production-scoped 2-hour simulation window (with agreed rollback criteria)

Attachments: fallback-terms-draft.docx, operational-simulations.pdf

Please review and tell us where you'd like firmer language or specific metrics. If procurement wants money-linked SLAs we'll have to route to commercial/legal for exceptions.

Regards,
Jordan
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@evergreenbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@evergreenbank.com
Date: 2026-10-12T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: fallback-binding terms and simulation plan (redwood)

Jordan — thanks, appreciate the clear draft. Procurement provided two small redlines: they want a maximum of 2 scheduled simulation windows per calendar year rolled into the terms and a template for evidence sharing (post-simulation report). They are ok with the operational framing and the caveats you listed.

Two quick asks before we move to redlines:
1) Can Redwood commit to producing a standard post-simulation report template we will use for evidence (latency graphs, failover time, checklist pass/fail)?
2) For the RPO language: can you add a line that clarifies durable persisted artifacts (transcripts/embeddings stored in customer-managed buckets) are restored according to customer's ingestion retention configuration — Redwood will provide assistance and exported snapshots on request.

If you can fold those into the draft we'll route redlines from procurement and move to DocuSign.

Best,
Carlos

--
